content.body:
This is actually the later model H-39 (French nomenclature makes no distinction), which was the original H-39 up-gunned just before the German invasion. This is an adequate light tank. It was 50% faster than the R-35 and well armored compared to its German opponents. Still, the 37 mm gun was inadequate to deal with anything substantial and the H-39 didn't achieve a notable degree of success. The low profile compared to heavier French tanks meant that it was a capable, if not stellar, ambusher. But its speed was really still too slow to get out of trouble in a hurry.
It does have a reasonable amount of armor, allowing it to shrug off light AT weapons. Good camouflage in some settings. Make sure you don't accidentally open the gunner's port. On other tanks, this would leave a very small vulnerability in the mantlet; on French tanks it opens a gaping port on the entire back of the turret leaving your turret members entirely exposed to even pistol fire.
Control Variations: Driver zooms in on view slit with (numpad 0 or Ins key). No periscope, closing view slit armor blocks view completely. Commander is in a cupola, cannot unbutton. View is through an armored view slit (key O to open). No view elevation change. View traverse speed limited to turret traverse speed. Gunner has an open viewport in front of him, non-closeable, unusable.
content.brief: TYPE: Light AFV ARMAMENT: 37 mm SA mle 38 L33 Gun 7.5 mm Reibel mle 1931 LMG WEIGHT: 12,000 kg SPEED: 36 km/h (road)
